review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped the uses of `d` and `ι_d` to see how the simp interface is used. The file has few simp lemmas of its own. The only recurring problem is that `d`, which is a def, has its defining property `ι_d` available only as a non-simp `@[reassoc]` lemma. Several proofs unfold `d` with `simp [d]` instead. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether making `ι_d` simp would change any existing proof, and the finding is hedged accordingly. I did not look for a dangerous orientation or a cycle, because `ι_d` rewrites `Sigma.ι _ m ≫ d g` to `g.hom m` and cannot loop.

findings.excerpt:
theorem ι_d {G A : C} {M : ModuleCat (End G)ᵐᵒᵖ} (g : M ⟶ ModuleCat.of (End G)ᵐᵒᵖ (G ⟶ A)) (m : M) :
    Sigma.ι _ m ≫ d g = g.hom m := by
  simp [d]
findings.problem: `d` is a def whose only interface lemma is `ι_d`, and `ι_d` is not a simp lemma. Downstream proofs therefore unfold the definition with `simp [d]`, which exposes `Sigma.desc` and its internals. `GabrielPopescu.preservesInjectiveObjects` does this at line 145 (`simpa [d] using! Sigma.ι _ ⟨f, hf⟩ ≫= hl`). The `kernel_ι_d_comp_d` proof also calls `ι_d` by hand (`simp only [Category.assoc, ι_d]`) and uses it reversed (`← ι_d g`). The canonical normal form `Sigma.ι _ m ≫ d g = g.hom m` (and `Sigma.ι _ m ≫ d g ≫ h = g.hom m ≫ h`) is not available to `simp` without unfolding `d`. This is a missing canonical simp lemma for a definition that is otherwise treated as opaque.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma as simp, `@[reassoc (attr := simp)] theorem ι_d ...`, so that both `ι_d` and `ι_d_assoc` are simp lemmas. Then replace `simpa [d] using! ...` at line 145 with a plain `simpa using! ...` that does not unfold `d`. Where unfolding `d` is truly needed, as at line 122 to match the shape of `epiDesc _ _ h`, keep it local. Rewriting `Sigma.ι _ m ≫ d g` to `g.hom m` is terminating and does not interact with any reverse rule. The only reverse use is the explicit `← ι_d g` at line 97, which is a manual rewrite and unaffected.
findings.benefit: Callers can simplify compositions `Sigma.ι _ m ≫ d g` without unfolding `d`. Proofs then no longer depend on `d` being implemented as `Sigma.desc`, so `d` can stay semi-opaque. It also gives a single canonical simp normal form, instead of each proof choosing between `simp [d]` and `simp only [ι_d]`.
